name: Bimetric Nonlocal MOND (BNM)
claimed_mechanism: We utilize Hassan-Rosen bigravity to supply a second dynamical metric, exiting the single-metric slip-lock theorem (DC-013). The bimetric interaction generates the necessary off-ray slip for lensing and a massive graviton. To achieve MOND dynamics, we introduce a spatially nonlocal elliptic operator that acts on the hidden metric sector, enforcing the F+ constraint dynamically without a preferred frame. This completely bypasses the P7 strong-coupling issues associated with single-metric screened preferred frames.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field limit, the massive graviton's helicity-0 mode dynamically tracks the acceleration scale, yielding MOND-enhanced dynamics. The nonlocal spatial operator enforces the exact mu=1-e^-y scaling of the acceleration, replacing the Yukawa profile of linear Hassan-Rosen bigravity. Because the slip originates from the bimetric difference rather than a preferred-frame vector, PPN lensing parameters satisfy gamma=1 and alpha_1=alpha_2=0 exactly.
inequivalence_argument: This candidate is inequivalent to DC-001, DC-012, and DC-013 because it abandons the single-metric requirement entirely, employing a second dynamical metric to evade the slip-lock theorem. It is inequivalent to DC-010 and DC-014 because it requires no preferred-frame vector, khronon, or timelike background field, entirely avoiding the P7 strong coupling and GW170817 constraints on the longitudinal mode. It is inequivalent to the closed nonlocal F+ pure-metric class because it pairs spatial nonlocality with a genuine second metric to solve the lensing slip problem, rather than relying on localization or frame-free diff-invariance.
